title: Toolflow SDKs: stream friction mitigation (draft)
body:
Summary:

This doc captures a lightweight PRD + implementation notes for reducing developer friction when integrating tool-calls and structured outputs into streaming flows from the Hosted API. Goal is to make the SDK ergonomics predictable across sync/async clients, reduce accidental data loss on client disconnects, and provide clear upgrade paths for existing customers using simple streaming today.

Problem statement (short):
- Developers building interactive experiences (chat UIs, code assistants, document synth tools) run into three recurring issues:
  1) ambiguous semantics for partial/structured frames when tool-calls are interleaved with free-text token streams;
  2) brittle reconnection/resume semantics that cause duplicate tool invocations or dropped outputs;
  3) mismatched client SDK behavior across languages (node/python/mobile) causing different developer expectations.

Key user scenarios we must support:
- Live chat with tool calls: client streams tokens while model asks for a web_search tool; client code wants a deterministic toolkit invocation lifecycle (invoke once, show intermediate progress, accept result).
- Progressive synthesis: model emits structured JSON blocks mid-stream (e.g., table rows) and client wants to render incrementally while validating shape.
- Mobile flaky networks: client must reconnect and resume the stream without re-triggering side-effects (no duplicate tool calls).
- Hybrid SDKs: sync server processes and browser SDKs must have both compatible default behaviors and clear knobs for advanced teams.

Design principles:
- Idempotency by default for tool invocation: wire a per-call id and require servers/clients to treat tool calls as idempotent unless explicitly labeled non-idempotent.
- Small, composable frame types: stream frames should be typed (text_delta, structured_frame, tool_request, tool_result, checkpoint) and include minimal routing metadata. Keep types stable but allow extensible metadata fields.
- Explicit client handshake for resume semantics: a lightweight session token + last-ack checkpoint allows resume without guessing offsets.
- Fail-safe default UI behavior: SDKs expose default handlers that "buffer until structured frame complete" for structured output and "show candidate progress" for tool calls, but allow opt-in low-latency mode that surfaces partial tool progress.

Proposed wire-level framing (informal):
- Every stream event is a JSON line with: {"type": "<frame>", "session_id": "<sid>", "seq": <n>, "payload": ... }
- Types: text_delta, structured_frame (json-schema-ref), tool_request (tool_id, call_id, inputs), tool_progress (call_id, progress_pct, partial_output), tool_result (call_id, exit_code, output), checkpoint (last_seq, snapshot_hash)
- Minimal size impact: text_delta frames remain compact; structured_frame includes small schema refs so clients can validate cheaply.

SDK ergonomics (per-platform notes):
- Node SDK: default streaming API returns AsyncIterable<Event>. Event includes helpers: .asText(), .asStructured(schemaValidator), .onTool(callHandler). Provide a convenience "dedupeTools: true" option that will automatic dedupe by call_id on reconnect.
- Browser SDK: streaming EventSource/Fetch streams must expose the same Event shapes. Add built-in reconnect with exponential backoff, and default checkpoint persistence in sessionStorage with opt-out.
- Python SDK: generator-based streaming with explicit resume(token) parameter. Provide a small adapter to convert Python generator into AsyncIterable for parity.
- Mobile (iOS/Android): recommend a lightweight wrapper that persists checkpoints to disk and exposes a delegate method for tool calls so app code can assert side-effect safeties.

Tool invocation lifecycle (recommendation):
1) Model emits tool_request with call_id. SDK emits onToolRequest(call_id, metadata).
2) Client code decides to accept or reject. If accepted, client returns a ToolHandle which the SDK maps to the call_id.
3) SDK forwards tool_progress frames to the ToolHandle while tool runs.
4) tool_result frame finalizes the call. On reconnect, SDK will check local call_id map and avoid re-invoking if result already observed.

Resume semantics and checkpoints:
- Checkpoints are authoritative for resume; they should include last_seq + minimal deterministic digest of the application-visible state (e.g., list of tool call_ids observed + last structured block ids).
- Server stores ephemeral session state for 5 minutes by default (configurable per-customer). If client reconnects within retention window and presents checkpoint, server will seek to next seq and deliver missing frames without re-emitting side-effect frames (tool_request should not be reissued; instead server replays tool_result if available).
- If checkpoint not found, server falls back to full rehydration behavior: socket restarts from beginning and client is encouraged to run reconciliation logic (we'll provide helper lib).

Backward compatibility & migration path:
- Existing streaming contracts will be supported with a transitional header flag: X-Redwood-Stream-Mode: legacy | typed. Default for new customers is "typed". For existing customers, they opt-in via console or request header.
- Server will map legacy bare text deltas into text_delta frames and inject synthetic checkpoints at sentence boundaries to minimize breakage.

Telemetry / observability requirements:
- Emit metrics: stream_connects, stream_resumes, resume_success_rate, duplicate_tool_invocations, tool_latency_p50/p95, structured_frame_parse_errors.
- Add structured logging for tool_request lifecycle with call_id, customer_id, model_id, and session_id. Logs should respect PII rules.

Security and safety considerations:
- Tool requests are potentially side-effecting. SDK default is to treat tool_request as non-executed until client explicitly authorizes. For low-latency integrated workflows (where model suggests a tool and app auto-invokes), require an explicit contract and enterprise opt-in.
- Tool payloads may contain sensitive data — mark tool frames as potentially confidential and prevent logging at DEBUG unless the customer explicitly enables.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How long should server session retention be for resume safety? (5m default proposed; longer for Dedicated customers.)
- Do we allow server-initiated dedupe for tools (so client can be truly dumb)? That would simplify mobile UX but increases server-side state complexity.
- Schema distribution: ship schema refs inline vs separate schema registry API? Inline increases payload; registry adds one more network hop. Hybrid approach possible: small inline hints + registry for full schema.

Implementation plan (90 day):
- Week 0-2: finalize frame format + language-neutral samples. Build spec doc and reference Node/py example libs.
- Week 3-6: Node + Python SDK changes (opt-in API). Add checkpoint persistence and reconnection helpers.
- Week 7-10: Server-side streaming route changes + session store prototype. Launch behind feature flag for internal testing.
- Week 11-12: QA with solutions-eng on 3 customer integrations (chat UI, document summarizer, mobile assistant).
- Week 13+: Gradual rollout, dashboards, and config knobs in Console.

Acceptance criteria (beta):
- SDKs expose new streaming event shapes and examples for tool flow.
- Reconnects with checkpoint succeed >= 95% internally for test suite.
- No duplicate tool invocations in the common case (client uses tooling as recommended).
- Telemetry surfaces duplicate_tool_invocations at < 1% for enabled customers.

Appendix: lightweight example (pseudo) - Node usage

const stream = client.stream({ model: 'gpt-redwood-7b', mode: 'typed' });
for await (const e of stream) {
  if (e.type === 'tool_request') {
    // return accepted or rejected to SDK
    stream.acceptTool(e.call_id, /* handler */ async (ctx) => {
      const result = await myWebSearch(ctx.inputs.q);
      return { output: result };
    });
  }
  if (e.type === 'structured_frame') {
    renderPartialTable(e.payload.rows);
  }
}

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: we want to ship sane defaults quickly for developers and iterate on advanced policies for Dedicated/Private.
- Please call out critical edge cases I may have missed (mobile disk limits, server memory limits if we keep long-lived tool maps, multi-tab clients).

Unresolved items to assign:
- retention-policy: owner @Ravi (decide default & per-customer override)
- schema-registry design: owner @Sofia
- QA test harness for duplicate invocation scenarios: owner @Miguel

-- end --
